user.title: Hot water tank
user.description: Pick the temperature sensor at the top of your hot water tank. A sensor near the bottom makes the estimate much smarter (it shows the cold water coming in while you shower).

data.name: Name
data.shower_temperature: Fixed shower temperature (only with 'Set it myself')
data.bathtub: There is a bath on this tank

data_description.tank_volume: Look on the type plate of the tank.
data_description.temperature_mode: Automatic: the model learns how much heat a minute of showering takes — nothing to fill in. Add your shower-head flow in the next step and it works out the temperature you shower at.
data_description.bathtub: Off when you only have showers and taps: filling a bucket or a sink fast is then never counted as a bath.

extras.title: Make it smarter (optional)
extras.description: These are suggested from the same device when possible. With them the model learns faster and more precisely. Leave empty if you do not have them.

data.heating_entity: Entity that shows the tank is being reheated
data.energy_sensor: Heat delivered to the hot water (energy sensor)
data.electricity_sensor: Electricity used for hot water (energy sensor)

data_description.profile: Where the model starts before it has learned from your own showers.
data_description.heating_entity: Without it, reheating is recognised from the temperature rising.
data_description.energy_sensor: Heat output for hot water (not electricity used). Lets the model learn how your tank layers.
data_description.flow_source: Optional. With the flow the integration works out the temperature you shower at and the litres. A water meter measures it while you shower. Don't know it? Choose 'Fill in myself' and measure it in a minute with a bucket (see below), or pick the type of shower head.
data_description.head_flow: Only with 'Fill in myself'. How to measure: turn the shower on the way you normally shower (same temperature and tap position), hold a bucket under the shower head and time how long it takes to fill 10 litres. Flow = 600 ÷ seconds: 50 s = 12 L/min, 75 s = 8 L/min, 100 s = 6 L/min. No marked bucket? Catch the water for 10 seconds, measure the litres with a measuring jug and multiply by 6. Measure twice and take the average.
data_description.water_sensor: A meter total (litres, m³) or a flow sensor (L/min). Recognises a shower live by a steady flow of water and makes its length exact; with 'Water meter' above it also measures the shower-head flow.
data_description.outdoor_sensor: Optional. Mains water follows the outdoor temperature with a delay of weeks; the model uses a 3-week average of it to estimate the cold water temperature. Without it, a monthly table is used.
data_description.electricity_sensor: Optional. Together with the heat sensor this lets the integration learn the COP for hot water.
data_description.cop: Leave empty to learn it from the heat and electricity meters (2.5 without them). Fill in to always use this COP: the heat pump's own COP for hot water, as its app shows it (electric boiler: 1.0).
data_description.price_sensor: Optional, choose your own (e.g. from your energy supplier or evcc). With dynamic tariffs the price at the moment the tank is reheated is used, not when you shower.
data_description.bathroom_sensor: Recognises a shower within a minute instead of after a few: a bathroom humidity sensor (rising), the power of the bathroom fan (running harder than usual), or a fan, light or motion sensor that switches on. Without it showers are told apart from washing up by how much heat they take, which takes a few minutes.

error.same_sensor: Top and bottom must be different sensors.

abort.already_configured: This tank is already set up.

error.same_sensor: Top and bottom must be different sensors.

sensor_missing.title: {name}: tank sensor not reporting
sensor_missing.description: The sensor {entity} has had no valid reading for more than two hours, so the shower time cannot be calculated. Check the device or integration that provides it.

sensors_swapped.title: {name}: top and bottom sensor swapped?
sensors_swapped.description: For more than six hours the bottom sensor has been more than 5 °C warmer than the top sensor while the tank was not being reheated. In a hot water tank the top is the warmest. Check whether {top} (top) and {bottom} (bottom) are the right way round in the integration's settings.

learning_failed.title: {name}: learning keeps failing
learning_failed.description: Learning from the history has failed {nights} nights in a row; the integration keeps using what it learned before. Please open an issue on GitHub and attach the diagnostics download.

heat_loss_raised.title: {name}: the tank loses more heat than it used to
heat_loss_raised.description: The tank's heat-loss coefficient is {recent} W/K, against {baseline} W/K before ({ratio}× as much). Possible causes: insulation that came loose or got wet, a pipe or circulation that now loses heat, or the tank standing somewhere colder. Showers and reheats are not counted: this is measured only while nothing happens.

possible_leak.title: {name}: possible dripping hot tap or leak
possible_leak.description:
While nobody used hot water, the bottom of the tank kept cooling faster than the top, night after night: the pattern of cold water slowly coming in. This points at a dripping hot water tap, a leaking thermostatic valve or safety valve, or a leak in the hot water pipes. Check the taps and the pipes.

Heat-loss coefficient now: {recent} W/K (usual: {baseline} W/K).
